newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen turning colder, wet on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen turning colder, wet on Wednesday.

text.p: Dry, warmer weather was expected to aid corn and soybean harvest progress in the U.S. Midwest on Tuesday but rain, followed by colder temperatures, was forecast for Wednesday and Thursday, meteorologists said.
"We're going to bring another system through the western corn belt on Wednesday," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
He forecast 0.10 to 0.50 inch with 50 percent coverage in the western corn belt. Central and southern Missouri will likely see the heaviest rains with accumulations up to 1.00 inch, he said.
Rains were expected to move eastward into Illinois on Wednesday afternoon and evening, continuing Thursday across much of the eastern corn belt, Palmerino said.
Colder temperatures will likely follow the rain with temperatures remaining colder through Saturday, said Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis.

"Skies will clear out in the western belt by late Wednesday and into the eastern belt by late Thursday," Davis said in his daily report. "Fair, dry and colder weather is on tap during the Thursday through Saturday period."
Long-range forecasts indicated a warm-up early next week with generally dry conditions, Palmerino said.
"It should be dry into the early part of next week with slowly warming temperatures," he said.
